$comment: STEP 1 of the layered extraction — the base reading. Nine fields, all read off the printed document without needing a domain judgement: is this a receipt, and who issued it. The other three steps are RESERVED artifacts (`desglose`, `rubro`, `clasificacion`); `test_the_extraction_steps_partition_every_field` proves the four together cover every field of the original 23-field contract exactly once. It carries no critical-severity field on purpose — the one field of group 1 that could only be CONFIRMED through an arithmetic combination (`importe_total_facturado`) moved to the step that holds that combination. The schema is a SEPARATE artifact from the prompt on purpose: the prompt says what to look for and how to read it, the schema says what shape the answer must have.

comprobante_valido.description: 'true' when the text is a readable receipt, 'false' when it is not

motivo_rechazo.description: Why the document was rejected, or 'null'

tipo_comprobante.description: the letter or the AFIP code printed in the header (001 Factura A, 006 Factura B, 011 Factura C), or 'null' when the document is not a fiscal receipt. 090/099 are 'comprobantes que no cumplen la RG 1415', not receipt classes

cuit_emisor.description: the emitter's CUIT, digits and its own hyphens only

moneda.description: the currency the document shows; 'ARS' when it shows none
